stories.headline: Fed raises rates for the first time since 2023, lifting the funds rate to 3.75%-4% and signaling more

key_facts.fact: The FOMC voted 12-0 on September 16 to raise the federal funds target range by a quarter point to 3.75%-4.00%, saying the move 'will support a timelier return' to its 2% inflation goal.
key_facts.excerpt: The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent... Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal.

key_facts.fact: It is the Fed's first rate increase in more than three years, the last having come in 2023, and it partially undoes one of last year's three cuts.
key_facts.excerpt: The Federal Reserve on Wednesday raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years in a renewed fight against inflation... Officials voted to raise their benchmark lending rate by a quarter point to a range of 3.75-4%, undoing one of last year's three rate cuts.

key_facts.fact: New projections show officials expect the policy rate in the 4.00%-4.25% range by the end of 2026 and unchanged at the end of 2027, implying at least one more hike this year.
key_facts.excerpt: New projections show officials see policy rate in 4.00%-4.25% range by end of 2026, unchanged at end of 2027

key_facts.fact: Chairman Kevin Warsh said the median projections put real GDP growth at 2.3% this year, total PCE inflation at 3.7% this year falling to 2.3% next year, and unemployment steady at about 4.1%; he again declined to submit a rate projection of his own.
key_facts.excerpt: In the Summary's median projections, real GDP rises at 2.3 percent this year and 2.4 percent next year. Total PCE inflation runs at 3.7 percent this year and falls to 2.3 percent next year. The unemployment rate holds steady at about 4.1 percent.

key_facts.fact: Reuters framed the decision as an acknowledgment that tariffs, the energy shock from the US-Israeli war with Iran and AI-boom capital spending have kept inflation too hot.
key_facts.excerpt: the combined impact of his global import tariffs, an energy shock following the start of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, and capital spending from the artificial intelligence boom has kept price pressures intense enough that the Fed felt it needed to raise its benchmark overnight interest rate by a quarter of a

key_facts.fact: The hike defies President Trump's demands for a cut; the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5% this week for the first time in three years, pulling mortgage rates up with it.
key_facts.excerpt: This week, the rate on the 10-year Treasury bond reached 5% for the first time in three years. Mortgage rates, which closely follow the 10-year Treasury, have also risen.

stories.headline: US House passes the Graham Russia and Iran sanctions bill 262-159 as Moscow fires 157 drones at Kyiv

key_facts.fact: The US House passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by 262-159; the measure targets Russian energy revenues and gives the White House tariff powers against major buyers of Russian oil and gas, and now heads to President Trump.
key_facts.excerpt: The measure, which passed 262-159 and now heads to President Donald Trump, targets Russian energy revenues and gives the White House tariff powers against major buyers of Russian oil and gas.

key_facts.fact: Hours after the vote, Russia struck Kyiv, Odesa and Zaporizhzhia overnight with ballistic and cruise missiles plus 157 drones; Ukraine's air force said it destroyed or suppressed 131 targets, but strikes hit 36 locations.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's air force said it destroyed or suppressed 131 Russian aerial targets during the overnight attack in the Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Odesa regions. The attack involved ballistic and cruise missiles as well as drones and decoys.

key_facts.fact: At least 19 people were injured, including a 10-year-old girl and a 12-year-old boy in Kyiv, where damage was recorded at more than 10 locations.
key_facts.excerpt: A Russian barrage of missiles and drones targeting Ukraine's capital and the surrounding region injured at least 19 people overnight and into Thursday morning, authorities said.

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces struck the Yaroslavl oil refinery and a military airfield in Rostov, damaging an An-12, two An-26s and three helicopters; Russia said it intercepted 641 Ukrainian drones overnight.
key_facts.excerpt: It claimed that Russian air defenses allegedly intercepted and destroyed 641 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones.

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy called it 'symbolic' that Congress passed the sanctions bill on the night of another Russian attack, and said sanctions are 'an extremely strong tool' that could push Moscow toward peace.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said it was "symbolic" that the US House of Representatives passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 amid another Russian ballistic missile and drone attack on Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: The exchange of energy strikes followed Trump's September 14 announcement of a Russia-Ukraine energy truce that neither side has confirmed.
key_facts.excerpt: The attacks that targeted energy facilities in Russia and Ukraine followed US President Donald Trump's announcement of an energy truce between the two countries on September 14, although neither side has confirmed such an agreement.

stories.headline: EU offers Canada an unprecedented 'associate member' status; Trump calls it a possible hostile act

key_facts.fact: In her State of the European Union address in Strasbourg on September 16, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed making Canada the EU's first associate member, telling Prime Minister Mark Carney she wanted to 'open the door'.
key_facts.excerpt: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday proposed making Canada the European Union's first associate member, a striking overture as U.S. President Donald Trump's threats drive Ottawa closer to Europe.

key_facts.fact: 'Associate membership' does not exist under EU treaties and has no binding definition in EU law; it is unclear who would approve it or how long it would take.
key_facts.excerpt: "Associate membership" does not currently exist in the EU structure and has no binding definition in EU law.

key_facts.fact: The plan would build on the existing CETA free-trade deal into an 'Alliance for the Future' covering advanced manufacturing, defense production, the Arctic, energy, critical minerals, batteries, AI, quantum computing and cybersecurity.
key_facts.excerpt: Von der Leyen said the expanded partnership would cover advanced manufacturing, technology, defense production, the Arctic, energy, critical minerals, batteries, artificial intelligence, quantum computing, cybersecurity and economic security.

key_facts.fact: Speaking in Charlotte, North Carolina, Trump called the prospect 'laughable', said it could be a 'hostile act' and threatened 'very heavy tariffs' on Europe in response.
key_facts.excerpt: Speaking in Charlotte, North Carolina, Trump suggested that allowing Canada to become an associate EU member could be a "hostile act" and threatened to respond to the proposed move by imposing more tariffs on the bloc.

key_facts.fact: Canada, which sends roughly 70% of its exports to the US, is in a tariff war with Washington after August's 50% US duties on some Canadian goods and Ottawa's dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs in September.
key_facts.excerpt: In August, the Trump administration enforced 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods, targeting dozens of products from hockey sticks to wine, after the U.S. and Canada failed to reach a trade deal. Canada responded with dollar-for-dollar counter-tariffs which went into effect in September.

key_facts.fact: Canada is not seeking full membership, which would mean surrendering sovereignty; details are expected to be settled at a Canada-EU summit in late October.
key_facts.excerpt: Wilkinson said Canada is not seeking full EU membership because it would require surrendering some sovereignty... He said the shape is likely to become clearer at the Canada-EU summit in October.

stories.headline: Oil gives back its spike as Saudi Arabia reroutes crude via Oman and moves to restore the East-West pipeline

key_facts.fact: Brent fell $1.24 (1.2%) to $104.59 and WTI dropped $1.14 to $101.29 in early Thursday trade, extending Wednesday's roughly $3 slide.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures fell $1.24, or 1.2 percent, to $104.59 a barrel by 00:49 GMT, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude declined $1.14, or 1.1 percent, to $101.29.

key_facts.fact: The retreat came after Saudi Arabia began offering extra crude loadings to Asian refiners through ship-to-ship transfers off Oman's Sohar port, easing fears of a Middle East supply squeeze.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia is offering more crude to Asian buyers through ship-to-ship transfers near Sohar, according to people familiar with the arrangements cited by Reuters.

key_facts.fact: Riyadh is seeking to restore about half the capacity of its damaged East-West pipeline within days and full operations within six weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia is seeking to return about half the capacity of its damaged East-West pipeline within days, and full operations in six weeks, a person familiar with the matter said.

key_facts.fact: Crude has rallied about three-quarters this year as the US-Iran war cut Middle East flows, and the surge in energy costs was among the pressures that pushed the Fed to hike rates on Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Crude has rallied by about three-quarters this year, as the US-Iran war cut Middle East flows and the Russia-Ukraine conflict drags on. Surging oil and fuel costs have fanned global inflationary pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates on Wednesday and signal more tightening.

key_facts.fact: Only three vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, against 12 the day before and a 10-day average of about 17, keeping a risk premium in the market.
key_facts.excerpt: As reported by Kpler, on Wednesday (6/26) only three (3) vessels transited through the Strait of Hormuz, compared to (12) the day before. On average, about 17 vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz over the last 10 days.

key_facts.fact: Brent had settled at $108.75 on Tuesday, a four-month high, after loadings were suspended at the Red Sea hub of Yanbu; it settled 2.7% lower on Wednesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Those developments sent crude sharply higher on Tuesday. Brent settled at $108.75 a barrel, while WTI rose to $105.83, as traders priced in the risk of prolonged disruption to one of Saudi Arabia's main alternative export routes.

stories.headline: SEC opens a five-year 'Innovation Exemption' letting on-chain venues trade tokenized US stocks

key_facts.fact: The SEC on September 17 issued an order, effective immediately, creating a regulatory pathway for certain trading venues to issue tokenized representations of publicly traded US stocks.
key_facts.excerpt: The Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday issued an order creating a regulatory pathway for certain trading venues to issue tokenized representations of publicly traded U.S. stocks, effective immediately.

key_facts.fact: The exemption gives qualifying platforms five years of relief from the exchange definition and gives liquidity providers five years of relief from dealer registration requirements.
key_facts.excerpt: Platforms trading tokenized stocks get five-year relief from exchange definition under SEC rules; Liquidity providers in tokenized stocks get five-year exemption from dealer registration requirements

key_facts.fact: Token holders must keep the same rights as traditional shareholders, including dividends and voting; companies can object to having their shares tokenized within a 30-day notice period and block the listing.
key_facts.excerpt: Trading platforms should notify the company of their intention to tokenize the shares and wait 30 days after the company receives the notice to start trading the token, according to an SEC spokesperson. If the company objects in that 30-day period, the trading venue can not make the tokenized stock available for trading

key_facts.fact: The order is a conditional regime for 'Tokenized Securities Venues', with ticker restrictions, volume caps tied to price-limit tiers and mandatory public disclosure of price, size, time, pool address and daily volume.
key_facts.excerpt: The exemption is designed as a controlled model, with ticker restrictions and volume caps based on price-limit tiers, and requires regular public disclosure of USD-denominated trading data, including price, size, time, pool address, end-of-day pool size, and daily trading volume

key_facts.fact: SEC Chair Paul Atkins said the interim measure 'must be followed by durable rulemaking', and it comes two days after the Senate blocked the Clarity Act crypto market-structure bill.
key_facts.excerpt: "Critically, this interim measure must be followed by durable rulemaking to ensure that onchain markets remain a viable pathway as our capital markets continue to evolve." ... The long-awaited move by the securities regulator comes two days after the Clarity Act, crypto's most consequential push for regulatory certainty, failed to advance in the Senate.

stories.headline: FDA clears Bayer's Kerendia for kidney disease in type 1 diabetes, the first advance there in 30 years

key_facts.fact: Bayer announced that the FDA approved KERENDIA (finerenone) to reduce urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio in adults with chronic kidney disease associated with type 1 diabetes, following Priority Review of a supplemental New Drug Application.
key_facts.excerpt: Bayer today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved KERENDIA (finerenone) to reduce urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR)... in adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD) associated with type 1 diabetes (T1D), following the agency's Priority Review of the supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA).

key_facts.fact: It is the first proven therapeutic advance in chronic kidney disease associated with type 1 diabetes in more than 30 years.
key_facts.excerpt: This approval is important for patients, as it is the first proven therapeutic advance in CKD associated with T1D in more than 30 years.

key_facts.fact: Approval rests on the Phase III FINE-ONE trial in 242 adults, where finerenone cut UACR versus placebo by 22% at three months and 28% at six months (p=0.0001).
key_facts.excerpt: At Month 3, KERENDIA reduced UACR compared to placebo by 22%... At Month 6, KERENDIA reduced UACR compared to placebo by 28% (ratio of LSGMR of 0.72; 95% CI: 0.60, 0.86).

key_facts.fact: Hyperkalemia occurred more often on the drug (10.1%) than placebo (3.3%), with 1.7% discontinuing because of it; overall adverse-event rates were similar to placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: Hyperkalemia, an adverse event of special interest, was observed more frequently with KERENDIA (10.1%) compared to placebo (3.3%). The rate of treatment discontinuation due to hyperkalemia was 1.7% and 0%, respectively.

key_facts.fact: Roughly 20-30% of people with type 1 diabetes in the US also have chronic kidney disease, putting them at risk of kidney failure.
key_facts.excerpt: Approximately 20-30% of people in the U.S. with T1D also have CKD, which puts them at risk of kidney disease progression and kidney failure.

stories.headline: SpaceX lofts a classified Space Force payload, six days before Starship's first orbital attempt

key_facts.fact: A Falcon 9 lifted off from Vandenberg's SLC-4E on Wednesday evening, September 16, with the classified USSF-259 payload, after a pre-fueling scrub on Tuesday; the booster landed on the droneship Of Course I Still Love You.
key_facts.excerpt: The company confirmed liftoff on X a few minutes after the four-hour window opened at 6:00 p.m. PT, then followed with a droneship recovery: Falcon 9's first stage landed on Of Course I Still Love You in the Pacific.

key_facts.fact: The payload is undisclosed but is presumed to be Starshield satellites, SpaceX's government-hardened Starlink variant, headed for a near-polar orbit inclined about 80 degrees.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Space Force has not publicly disclosed full details about the satellites carried by the mission. However, the payload is presumed to include satellites from Starshield, SpaceX's satellite network designed to provide secure communications and other capabilities for government and military users.

key_facts.fact: It was Falcon 9's 106th mission of 2026 and the third classified Space Force launch from the same pad in just over a month, under an NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 ceiling the Space Force raised from $5.6B to $17B in July.
key_facts.excerpt: Tonight's flight will be Falcon 9's 106th mission of 2026... The mission is the third classified Space Force satellite launch SpaceX has executed in just over a month from a single pad

key_facts.fact: SpaceX has set September 22 for Starship Flight 14, the program's first attempt at a closed orbital trajectory: roughly six orbits at 275 km over about 10 hours, ending in a Pacific splashdown west of Chile.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX is targeting Sept. 22, 2026, for the first orbital flight of its Starship launch system, a roughly 10-hour mission that will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites and send the spacecraft around Earth six times before a planned Pacific Ocean splashdown.

key_facts.fact: Flight 14 carries 26 operational Starlink V3 satellites — three fitted with cameras aimed at the heat shield — and, per CFO Bret Johnsen, will be Starship's first revenue-generating flight; an FAA license was still pending.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen told investors at Goldman Sachs' Communacopia and Technology Conference on September 10 that Flight 14 will be "a revenue-generating flight," specifically because it will carry 26 production Starlink V3 satellites to an operational orbit

key_facts.fact: All 13 previous Starship flights were deliberately suborbital; reaching orbit is the prerequisite for the propellant-transfer campaign NASA's Artemis lunar landing depends on.
key_facts.excerpt: This will be the first Starship flight to aim for a closed orbital trajectory rather than a suborbital arc. Every prior flight — including Flight 13's July 24 Indian Ocean splashdown — followed a ballistic path
